subject: ss-endocrinology
title: Cardiovascular and renal outcome trials in diabetes

steps.tx: **EMPA-REG OUTCOME** tested empagliflozin in type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease. It reduced 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events, cardiovascular death, and hospitalisation for heart failure. The mechanism drawing shows gut incretin beside a beta cell and a blocked tubular glucose cotransporter. No event curve and no FLOW result are on that figure.
steps.say: EMPA-REG OUTCOME tested empagliflozin in type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease. It reduced 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events, cardiovascular death, and hospitalisation for heart failure. vis.alt: Intestinal incretin beside a pancreatic beta cell, and a proximal renal tubule with the glucose cotransporter blocked.
vis.caption: Incretin from the gut is drawn beside the pancreatic beta cell. The proximal tubule is drawn with the glucose cotransporter blocked. No event curve and no FLOW result are on this figure (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **CANVAS showed** that canagliflozin reduced major adverse cardiovascular events. An amputation signal was reported, and it is not treated as a class effect, but the feet are still examined before and during treatment. A patient with an active foot ulcer needs a foot plan before canagliflozin is started. The signal does not cancel the cardiovascular result.

steps.tx: **DECLARE-TIMI** 58 tested dapagliflozin. It was noninferior for major adverse cardiovascular events, and it reduced hospitalisation for heart failure. Many participants had no prior cardiovascular disease, so the heart-failure result is not limited to secondary prevention. This population is different from EMPA-REG OUTCOME.

steps.tx: **LEADER showed** that liraglutide reduced 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events. SUSTAIN-6 showed that injectable semaglutide also reduced those events, and a retinopathy signal was reported. A rapid fall in glucose is watched when advanced eye disease is present. Name the drug and the trial, because the class is not one result.

steps.tx: **REWIND showed** that dulaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events. Most participants did not have established cardiovascular disease, which is the point that separates this trial from a secondary-prevention-only study. A once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist can be the cardiovascular choice in that broader group. Glucose lowering is not the endpoint that carried the result.

steps.tx: **CREDENCE showed** that canagliflozin reduced kidney failure and cardiovascular events in albuminuric chronic kidney disease with type 2 diabetes. DAPA-CKD and EMPA-KIDNEY extended the kidney benefit to people with or without diabetes. The class-effects drawing marks kidney events and cardiovascular benefit for SGLT2 inhibitors, and only major cardiovascular events for GLP-1 receptor agonists.

vis.alt: Class-effects drawing. SGLT2 inhibitors are marked with reduced major kidney events and a cardiovascular benefit. GLP-1 receptor agonists are marked only with fewer major adverse cardiovascular events. FLOW is not named on the drawing.
vis.caption: As drawn, SGLT2 inhibitors cover kidney events and cardiovascular benefit, and GLP-1 receptor agonists cover major cardiovascular events only. The FLOW kidney result for semaglutide is in the text and is not on this drawing.

steps.tx: **FIDELIO** showed that finerenone reduced a kidney composite in patients already on RAS blockade. FIGARO-DKD showed a reduction in cardiovascular events. Hyperkalemia is the main hazard, and the potassium is checked. Finerenone is not an SGLT2 inhibitor, and it is considered when albuminuria persists on a RAS blocker.

steps.tx: **SELECT showed** that semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in people with overweight or obesity and cardiovascular disease who did not have diabetes. FLOW showed that semaglutide slowed kidney progression in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease. FLOW is in the text, and it is not named on the class-effects drawing.
